subject: Processor evidence escrow, routing proposal and TIA timestamping
messages:
From: Sara Byrne <sara.byrne@medisec.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>
Cc: Katherine Lee <katherine.lee@novamed.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Mar 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Medisec: processor evidence / escrow ask for SCCs + UK Addendum

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for taking this. We're starting the DPA/TIA work for Medisec's EU–UK deployment and have a couple of questions where we need a concrete proposal from Redwood on how you intend to:

- Stage subprocessor evidence in an auditable escrow (for procurement/infosec review)
- Provide cryptographically timestamped attestations (so evidence can't be backdated) to satisfy our DTIA/TIA requirements
- Route processing (onshore fallback) if a subprocessor fails the attestation

Attached is our initial SCT/TIA questionnaire and a short list of priority subprocessors. Can you outline a draft approach and rough timeline? Our legal and procurement teams will need a short write-up to move the UK Addendum sign-off.

Attachments: Medisec_TIA_questionnaire.xlsx (attached)

Best,
Sara Byrne
Head of Data Procurement
Medisec Health

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Sun, 1 Mar 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Medisec: processor evidence / escrow ask for SCCs + UK Addendum

Hi Sara — thanks for the questionnaire and priority list. Looping in Laura (legal) and Marissa (privacy) for formal responses, and I sketched a pragmatic three-phase proposal below so procurement has something concrete while we align on contract language.

High level proposal (draft):
1) Mapping sprint (1–2 weeks): map Medisec's priority subprocessors to SCC clauses and UK Addendum dependencies; identify evidence buckets (SOC2 summary, KMS attestation, ingress/egress diagrams).
2) Evidence escrow staging (2–4 weeks): Redwood publishes hashed manifests of each subprocessor evidence bundle into a tamper-evident escrow store. The store will retain signed manifests plus retrieval metadata; we will provide a retrieval API for auditors.
3) Timestamped DTIA/TIA (ongoing): each evidence bundle gets an HSM-backed signature and RFC 3161-compatible timestamp token. Combined with the hashed manifest this gives a verifiable, non-repudiable timeline.

Key assumptions and asks from Medisec:
- Confirm which subprocessors require UK onshore fallback vs. EU-only routing.
- Confirmation on retention window for escrowed evidence (we propose 24 months by default).

I attached a short spreadsheet that lays out the escrow schema, manifest fields and retrieval SLAs. Laura/Marissa — any contractual or privacy redlines we should pre-empt for the UK Addendum / SCC mapping?

Attachments: processor-escrow-schema.xlsx

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.inference>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>
Cc: Sara Byrne <sara.byrne@medisec.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Sun, 1 Mar 2026 14:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Medisec: processor evidence / escrow ask for SCCs + UK Addendum

Thanks Ben / Sara. A few legal-level clarifications so procurement can avoid scope creep:

- Language: prefer term "evidence escrow" rather than "escrow" alone (financial escrow has different connotations).
- Access model: Redwood will provide access to Medisec and appointed auditors via pre-authorized retrieval tokens; any third-party auditor access must be limited by DPA appendix and logged.
- UK Addendum: counsel will need explicit fallback routing clauses. Specifically, if a UK-jurisdiction subprocessor fails attestation, we should offer (a) onshore processing fallback where feasible, (b) contractual remedy windows, and (c) documented roll-back of data flows. Those mechanics should be captured as an annex to the DPA.

I have a couple of redline points on the SCC mapping (I'll attach a short note). Also note: we should avoid exchanging raw logs that contain customer data in the escrow — only metadata and hashed manifests.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachment: uk-idta-addendum-notes.docx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>

Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Medisec: processor evidence / escrow ask for SCCs + UK Addendum

Hi Sara — quick privacy points to align with Laura's legal notes:

- Evidence types: we will curate the following minimal evidence set per subprocessor: SOC2 Type II summary (redacted where necessary), KMS/HSM attestation, network flow diagrams (high level), and a signed subprocessor statement of processing.
- Retention & minimization: escrow will store only hashed bundles and retrieval metadata. Raw evidence will be stored encrypted and only released to named auditors on request; we propose a 24-month default retention, with options to shorten to 12 months for specific customers.
- Split the TIA work: technical/cryptographic assurances (DTIA) vs. contractual guarantees (UK Addendum). We'll own the DTIA design and provide a one-page TIA primer for procurement.

Attaching the privacy checklist we typically give to procurement teams.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Privacy & Product Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachment: TIA_evidence_checklist.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>

Subject: Re: Medisec: processor evidence / escrow ask for SCCs + UK Addendum

Marissa / Ben / Sara — a few technical notes on the DTIA/timestamping design:

- Timestamping: propose an HSM-backed signing flow that emits a signed manifest and an RFC 3161-style timestamp token. The escrow store will keep the manifest hash and the timestamp; auditors can fetch the manifest and verify the HSM signature and timestamp chain.
- Proof-of-possession: we will store an HSM attestation (vendor-signed) for our signing key and provide a short verification path (JWS + certificate chain).
- Encryption & access: raw evidence bundles encrypted with customer-specific KEKs; escrow holds only encrypted blobs + manifest metadata. Retrieval requires a two-party token (requestor + Medisec approval) to reduce risks.
- Retrieval SLA: propose 48-hour standard retrieval for audits, 8-hour expedited for critical legal holds (subject to contract).

I added a short appendix to the escrow schema spreadsheet with fields for: manifest_id, hash_algo, timestamp_token_b64, hsm_key_id, retention_until, retrieval_sla.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Security Architect, Serving Platform
